# Lumber Hall: a timber wholesaler's market hall, through the block

Identity: a twin-gabled half-timbered burgage warehouse (Hanseatic Speicher type) running from the north street to
the south street. Each street sees the same face: two great slate gables, each with stacked loading doors and a
hoist beam at the apex, jettied twice over a ground-floor row of three wood merchants (a Folio plus its door
stalls each). One wood per business, shown in its own logs, planks and leaves. Stair lobby at the west end and a
cart passage through the block at the east end.

## SITE

Plot x 0..42, z 0..37. Front = NORTH (-z), x runs along the street. Mirror rule: the south face is the north face
reflected about z = 18.5 (z -> 37 - z).

# Lumber Hall: a timber wholesaler's market hall, through the block

Identity: a twin-gabled half-timbered burgage warehouse (Hanseatic Speicher type) running from the north street to
the south street. Each street sees the same face: two great slate gables, each with stacked loading doors and a
hoist beam at the apex, jettied twice over a ground-floor row of three wood merchants (a Folio plus its door
stalls each). One wood per business, shown in its own logs, planks and leaves. Stair lobby at the west end and a
cart passage through the block at the east end.

## SITE

reflected about z = 18.5 (z -> 37 - z).

input.summary:
parts/frame.mjs builds the first-floor and loft timber frame on both faces and both sides: bays from plan FACADES (posts, mann/brace/window/door fills, door lintels), jetty brackets y11 and y17, head plates y17 and cornice y23, side walls with posts every 4, hoist beams and hoods, and the four gable frames.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the Timber frame line shows 1726 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Front render reads as Tudor half-timber with two gables and jetties.
Ticked P2 in plan.md, three elements.md items (jetties, gables, hoist beams), and added P2 notes to plan.md.

waste.what: Worked out every bay's x-span, post and air column by hand against the plan's bay table, then mirrored each storey for the south face by hand.
waste.cost: about 10 minutes of reasoning and two rewrites of the bay list
waste.tool: A frame helper that takes a face's bay table (plan FACADES) and builds a storey on either street by mirrorZ, with the post rhythm and door/window columns as data.

waste.what: Side walls written cell by cell with g.set in nested loops, skipping window cells by hand.
waste.cost: about 2 x 28 x 6 g.set calls in a loop, with overlap checks against the front bays done by reading the plan
waste.tool: A wallX/wallZ-style helper in vocab with posts-at-list and openings-as-data, shared with shell.mjs, which already has the same loops.

waste.what: Checked the frame line in the parts report and render by eye only; no check that window and door openings are left open for P5 or that the gable doors avoid the king posts.
waste.cost: one render, one zoom, two reads of the report
waste.tool: mcd check should flag cells a later part needs open (openings in plan OPENINGS) when the frame fills them.

companions.task: Set the window panes (1x2 glass at x7, 19, 23, 35 on both upper storeys, and the side windows at z 7, 19, 31) and the shutters, which need air in the bay's outer columns that the frame has filled with calcite.
Hang the gable loading doors at y25..27 on x11..12 and x30..31 and settle the conflict with the king posts there, and check the hoist hoods against the roof's overhang at z2.

left: Windows, glass and shutters (P5): the window bays keep only the middle column open, so windowUnit's shutters at x6/x8 land on calcite and will be refused; open the outer columns or put the shutters in the plan's fittings.

Gable loading doors at y25..27 on x11..12 and x30..31 (P5) collide with the gable king posts that gableFrame builds there; the doors will be refused unless the king posts move or the doors are dropped.
Loft and first-floor loading doors (P5): the frame leaves x11..12 and x30..31 open at the door bays and adds lintels at y16 and y22; the doors' transoms (y15, y21) and the leaves are P5's.
Side windows (x2 and x40) are left as air at z 7, 19, 31 for P5 to glaze, not placed here; plan's z 9, 21, 29 are posts, so the deviation is noted in plan.md.
The loft and first-floor timber store items in elements.md stay unticked until P5 adds their windows and loading doors.

Walkability and the stair hall/loft interior were not checked by me; mcd check reported no floating or unsupported blocks from the frame. The 24 orphan smooth_stone_slab blocks in the check output come from another part (counters), not the frame.
